rationale: CONFIRMED P1 stale protected-validation reuse in local.closeout_local, not merely an untested hypothesis. Independent tiny fixture first records a passed validation adapter running an actual Ruff command. Ignored .ruff.toml then changes to an incompatible required-version; an independent fresh Ruff command exits2. An unchanged result/base/files subject nevertheless reuses the old passed record with only one closeout validation dispatch, sets publication_eligible=True and creates an ordinary feature commit. No actual production protected gate or remote/main write was fabricated: the constrained adapter is explicitly labeled INDEPENDENT_SINGLE_REAL_RUFF_CHECK_NOT_PROTECTED_GATE. The real cache consumer and Git commit are exercised. Existing scoped CodingCommands controls independently reject changed tests/config/runner/declared dependency/selector and retain freshness for unrelated evidence; tracked-tree guards are useful but do not close ignored/toolchain/environment inputs. Bounded next repair: refuse unsafe reuse until a supported exact validation-input profile exists, or require fresh protected validation before commit. Bind executable/check selector, relevant inputs, toolchain/environment assumptions and declared exclusions; unknown/older profiles cannot silently qualify. Add ignored-config drift, fresh failure, unchanged reuse and irrelevant-file controls. Separately qualify HEAD-sensitive validation: integration validates working bytes before committing; tree equality alone does not prove HEAD/worktree-sensitive tests or external inputs equivalent. No universal filesystem read tracer, validator framework, gate weakening or retrospective receipt rewrite. Preserve source/review/task/grant boundaries; future repair needs explicit implementation scope.
